html:
The Pocomoke were an Algonquian-speaking people of the Pocomoke River on the Eastern Shore of the Chesapeake Bay, on the border of today's Maryland and Virginia. They lived in villages by the river and the marshes, farming maize and fishing, much like their neighbours the Accomack and the Nanticoke.

English settlers moved onto the Eastern Shore from the 1620s, and over the next century most Pocomoke land passed to colonists. Families of Pocomoke descent still live in the area. See also Powhatan, the chiefdom across the bay.
